title: L116 — THE CLOSE THAT DECIDED MONDAY
_cellule: OITD (Circuit) · Autorité · Nightmare · regard=autres traders · futur · −−
voice: You closed your laptop on Friday afternoon with a trade still open, because the chart looked fine and the weekend felt short.
The market you trade closes at five, but the news that moves it does not stop publishing at five.
When the market reopened, the price jumped past your stop and filled at the next available order, which was nowhere near the level you had chosen.
The gap did not break your stop, it skipped it entirely, because a stop is a request to sell at a price that no longer exists.
A stop only works when someone is there to buy it. Follow KONGRAVE — the mechanics nobody explains.

caption:
You closed your laptop on Friday with a trade still open, because the chart looked fine and the weekend felt short.

The market closes at five, but the news that moves it does not stop at five. When it reopened, the price jumped past your stop and filled at the next available order — nowhere near the level you chose.

A stop only works when someone is there to buy it.
